# A program the oracle answers that ISO 7185 does not admit leaves the denominator, named here with its clause and its measurement. SCRIP refuses it, and the refusal is the ISO answer (CEO-1225: ISO wins where fpc -Miso is lax; the Pascal skill: never adopt -Miso's laxity).

column3: ISO 7185 6.8.3.9 ("Neither a for-statement nor any procedure-and-function-declaration-part of the block that closest-contains a for-statement shall contain a statement threatening the variable denoted by the control-variable"): readvocab declares I (line 174) and its nested procedure GETLTR (line 194) assigns I:=I+1 (line 196), while readvocab's own FOR I:=65 TO 90 (line 214) is the for-statement the clause protects; SCRIP refuses at parse, rc 1, no output: "ISO 7185 6.8.3.9 violation in advfls.pas line 214: for-statement control-variable 'i' is threatened at line 196 ... in procedure readvocab"; fpc -Miso 3.2.2 compiles it rc 0 and the recorded answer src/fpc/advfls.out is its two lines, and fpc -Mfpc compiles it rc 0 too, so no fpc mode enforces the clause here and the ref rests on the oracle's laxity, not an answer; the entry's dialect is iso (no mode directive, nothing forcing objfpc), so SCRIP's check stands; measured by senior_05 2026-11-12 on SCRIP at corpus ba505e7e3 (first found by junior_03, row advpas350-red-src-fpc-advfls)
